s_open.name: 14:55, Wednesday
s_open.title: 14:55, Wednesday
s_open.body:
You are covering a shift for Danni, who called in sick.

Rachel, 24. She works Wednesdays at a garden centre on the north side of town. You are rostered to collect her at 3:00 and drive her to physio at 3:30.

You have never met her.

You are in the car park. The only thing you have is last week's note.

s_note.name: The note
s_note.title: Last Wednesday's note
s_note.body:
Took Rachel to work. All good. She seemed a little tired in the car.

That is the whole note.

q_arrive.name: She is not out front
q_arrive.title: Rachel is not at the front entrance
q_arrive.body:
It is 2:55. The roster says front entrance. There are two staff having a smoke by the door and no sign of Rachel.

Physio is a twelve minute drive.

What do you do?

choices.label: Wait in the car — she will come out

s_wait.name: You wait
s_wait.title: You wait in the car
s_wait.body:
You wait. At 3:05 you get out and walk to the front doors.

Rachel has been sitting on a pallet by the loading door at the back since two o'clock. She always waits there. The front entrance is loud and there is nowhere to sit.

You leave at 3:20. Physio has a fifteen minute grace period. You do not make it.

s_inside.name: You go inside
s_inside.title: You go inside and ask
s_inside.body:
A supervisor points you round the back without looking up. "She'll be on the pallet by the loading door. She's always there."

Rachel has been waiting since two. She finished early today.

You make physio with three minutes to spare.

Nobody wrote any of this down. You found out because you asked a stranger.

s_office.name: You ring the office
s_office.title: You ring the office
s_office.body:
Someone in the office answers and opens the file while you wait.

The note says what you have already read.

She rings the garden centre, then rings you back at 3:09. Rachel waits at the loading door. She finished at two today.

The office has now spent nine minutes on a question that a single line in a note would have answered.

q_note.name: Your turn to write
q_note.title: You are writing your own note now
q_note.body:
Next Wednesday somebody covers Rachel. It might be Danni. It might be someone who has never met her.

Which of these would you write?

choices.label: "Collected Rachel from work and drove her to physio. All went well."
choices.feedback: "All went well" is your judgement, and the next worker cannot act on it. They still will not know where she waits, or that she sometimes finishes at two.

choices.label: "Rachel waits on the pallet by the loading door at the back, not the front entrance. She finished at 2:00 today and had been waiting. Collected her at 3:05 and drove her to physio."
choices.feedback: This is the one. Where she waits, when she finished, what you did. The next worker walks straight round the back and Rachel does not sit on a pallet for an hour.

choices.label: "Rachel was annoyed about being kept waiting again."
choices.feedback: "Annoyed" is what you concluded, not what you saw — and it puts the problem on Rachel rather than on the missing information. The next worker now meets an annoyed woman before they meet Rachel.

s_end.name: Debrief
s_end.title: There was no good option at 2:55
s_end.body:
Waiting cost Rachel her appointment. Ringing the office cost the office nine minutes. Asking a stranger worked, and you should not have had to.

None of that was your mistake. The information you needed was never written down.

Last Wednesday somebody had a few minutes at the end of a long day and wrote eleven words.

Next Wednesday, yours is someone else's.

Here is what could have been written in the same few minutes:

Drove Rachel to the garden centre for her 9:00 start. Rachel waits at the loading door at the back when she finishes, not the front entrance. Some Wednesdays she finishes at 2:00 instead of 3:00 — check with her supervisor. Collected her at 3:05 and drove her to physio.

Same shift. Same few minutes. Three headings.
